tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill for...') and lists explicit trigger contexts (Xid/ECC errors, slow training, FSx slowness, NCCL hangs, NVLink/Fabric Manager errors, nodes in Failure/Pending, mass termination, readiness questions). It focuses on outcomes the user cares about (evidence coverage, node verdicts, pre-flight readiness) rather than internal implementation details, and while dense, it stays within a reasonable paragraph length appropriate for a complex, multi-scenario skill.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), ParallelCluster, or self-managed EC2/EKS GPU instances... Activate on Xid or ECC errors, slow training or FSx for Lustre slowness on a GPU cluster, NCCL hangs or TCP fallback, NVLink or Fabric Manager errors, nodes in Failure or Pending, nodes terminating at once, or 'is my cluster ready for a multi-day run'."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense with cluster-specific, non-obvious facts (API names, event names, Capacity Block termination timing, Xid classification rules) rather than generic explanations of what GPUs or logs are. It does not waste space on concepts the agent already knows.
tests.evidence: R3. Node identity survives replacement. A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace gives the node a new instance ID in the same instance group...
